description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

PERL 5.36+: `use feature 'extra_paired_delimiters'` (experimental) adds a set
of PAIRED delimiters to the quote-like operators beyond `() [] {} <>` -- the
Unicode bracket pairs, so `qÂ«textÂ»`, `qqãtextã`, `mâ¨patâ©` and their nesting
work, and the closing delimiter must match the opening one.  Outside the
feature's lexical scope the same spellings are ORDINARY characters, so a
program that uses one there is a syntax error -- which is what the test file
asserts in both directions.

PCL: the feature is nowhere in the tree (grepped: no `extra_paired` in
docs/, lib/ or Pl/).  PPI's lexer is asked with PCL's feature state
(`custom_feature_include_cb`, #360), so the delimiters are not recognised and
the in-scope rows fail; the out-of-scope rows, which assert a FAILURE, fail
too (PCL does not validate -- principle 9).

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/lex.t
  37 `Various tests of string delims \xAB/\xBB returned without error`
  38 `And the expected number of warnings were generated`
  39 `And the first warning is as expected`
  40 `And the second warning is as expected`
  41 `And the third warning is as expected`
  42 `Using paired delimiter both fore/aft fails as expected`
  44 `Using extra paired delimiter outside scope fails as expected`
  46 `Reversing delimiters works, as expected within scope of extra delims`
  48 `Using terminating paired delimiter fore, opening aft fails as expected outside scope of extra delims`
  50 `Using nested extra paired delimiters works`
  52 `Using too few closing delims in nesting fails as expected`
(t/op/lex.t lines 314-380; 11 of the file's 41 blessed rows.)

SHAPE: the WORK is PPI's, not PCL's -- PPI 1.291 has no
`extra_paired_delimiters` support, so the tokens do not arrive.  Check what
PPI does with `qÂ«aÂ»` before designing anything here; if PPI mis-lexes it (as
opposed to refusing the document) that is a rule-13 upstream log.  The rows
that assert a FAILURE (42, 44, 48, 52) are principle 9 and belong to
`NS:Error compatibility for invalid Perl input` whatever happens to the
feature; the three warning rows are #221.

So the honest split is: 4 rows NS:invalid-input, 3 rows #221, 4 rows this
task.  Registered as one task because a reader looking at op/lex.t needs one
pointer.
subject: use feature 'extra_paired_delimiters' (5.36) is absent -- PPI 1.291 does not lex the Unicode bracket pairs, so 11 op/lex.t rows fail (4 of them principle-9 invalid-input rows and 3 of them #221)
